principle: Commercial labels are context objects and hypotheses. They do not become psychological nodes unless independently supported as scientific constructs.

dimensions.name: Audience & Situation
dimensions.purpose: Who is acting, in what situation, with what knowledge/context.

dimensions.name: Goals, Jobs & Desired Outcomes
dimensions.purpose: What outcome the audience is trying to achieve or avoid.
not_equivalent_to: active goal representation unless currently evidenced

dimensions.name: Problems, Barriers & Costs
dimensions.purpose: What blocks progress or makes current state costly.
not_equivalent_to: perceived motivational cost unless recipient-side evidence exists

dimensions.name: Product & Capability
dimensions.purpose: What the product can actually do, how, and under what limitations.

dimensions.name: Alternatives & Status Quo
dimensions.purpose: What the audience can choose instead, including doing nothing.

dimensions.name: Value Hypotheses
dimensions.purpose: Candidate ways the product creates value relative to goals, alternatives and sacrifices.
not_equivalent_to: subjective task value until receiver-side evidence exists

dimensions.name: Risk, Objections & Belief Gaps
dimensions.purpose: Reasons the audience may reject, delay or doubt.

dimensions.name: Friction & Action Path
dimensions.purpose: Practical burdens between interest/intention and completed action.

dimensions.name: Proof & Evidence Inventory
dimensions.purpose: Available support for claims and its traceability/diagnosticity.

dimensions.name: Customer Language
dimensions.purpose: Verbatim language, concepts, objections, metaphors and category terms used by the audience.
not_equivalent_to: common ground or connotation unless contextualized

dimensions.name: Market & Category Context
dimensions.purpose: Competitive/category conventions, sophistication, norms, substitutes and expectations.
not_equivalent_to: descriptive norm unless referent and perception are evidenced
